inputs.original_text: Bloomberg: “Every day, as energy prices rise, flights are canceled and death and destruction fill screens, people across the world ask when the Iran war — widely viewed as poorly planned, unwinnable and a peril to global well-being — will stop.” “Not in Israel, where the public is strongly behind seeing the war through until [...]
inputs.modified_text: Bloomberg is trying to frame the chaos from rising energy prices and the war against Iran as proof that the world needs to end this badly planned conflict right away for the sake of global stability. Yet the account concedes that Israelis are standing firmly behind continuing the fight, spinning it as real national strength triumphing over weak global hand-wringing and progressive calls for disorder. What this really reveals is how some voices are weaponizing public resolve to prop up militaristic approaches that deepen inequality and sideline the needs of vulnerable populations caught in the crossfire. These wars are sustained by entrenched power structures that prioritize domination over equitable solutions, and we should be demanding institutional reforms and diplomatic paths that protect human lives and address the structural harms instead of celebrating endless escalation.
